The sky appears blue because sunlight is made up of all colors, and as it passes through the atmosphere, air molecules scatter shorter wavelengths (blue and violet) much more strongly than longer ones—a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering. Although violet light is scattered even more than blue, our eyes are more sensitive to blue and some violet is absorbed higher in the atmosphere, so we perceive the sky as blue. At sunrise and sunset, light travels through more atmosphere, scattering away the blue and leaving reds and oranges visible.
